page.layout: One page of text with a woodcut ornament and historiated initial; line numbers printed in the right margin (10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40) beside the text; no left margin text. Top: page number above the ornament. Then title block (centred), then body text, then a second section headed PROLOGVS LIBRI II, ending with catchword PRO- at the foot.

main_text.head: LIBER HISTORIARVM PHILIPPICARVM, ET TOTIVS MVNDI origines, & terræ situs.
main_text.p: 10PRIMO volumine continentur hæc, Imperium Assyriorum à Nino rege, vsque ad Sardanapalum. Post quem translatum est per Arbactum ad Medos, vsq; ad vltimum regem Astiagen. 20Is à nepote suo Cyro pulsus regno: & Persæ regno potiti. Vt Croeso Lydiæ regi bellum intulit Cyrus; victumque cepit. Hic in excessu dicti Æolicarum & Ionicarum vrbium situs; originesque Lydorum, & in Italia Tuscorum. Post Cyrum, filius Cambyses Ægyptum in domuit. Repetitæ Ægypti origines vrbium. Extinc-to Cambyse, Darius occisis Magis regnum Persicum accepit; captaque Babylone, bella Scythica molitus est.
main_text.head: PROLOGVS LIBRI II.
main_text.p: 30SEcundo volumine continentur hæc; Scythiæ & Ponti situs; originesque Scythiæ, vsque ad bellum quo est inde pulsus Darius: qui post hanc fugam Græciæ bellum intulit, per Datin & Tisafernem, quod soli Athenienses tenuere. Hic origines Athenarum repetitæ, & reges vsque 35ad Pisistrati tyrannidem, qua extincta vicere Persas. Vt, mortuo Dario filius Xerxes bellum Græciæ intulit: ac repetitæ origines Thessaliæ: expulsoque Græcia Xerxe bellum ab Athenienfibus translatum in Asiam, vsque ad Xerxis interitum. 40

page.notes: Woodcut ornament at top and historiated initial D; the printed page number 310 is at the head. Right-margin line numbers 10–40 are marginal line markers. Some words in the body are faint or show-through; "Croeso" read as Crœso and "Datin" as Datis are uncertain; "Ægyptum in domuit" likely "in domum". Catchword PRO- at foot.
